name: Reacquisition of Romanian Citizenship (Former Citizens and Descendants, Articles 10-11)

qualifying_event.description: A former Romanian citizen who lost citizenship while acquiring/retaining a foreign nationality (Article 10), or a person from whom citizenship was taken away or who lost it for reasons not attributable to them -- chiefly through 20th-century territorial changes affecting historical Romanian territory (Bessarabia, Bukovina, Northern Transylvania, Southern Dobruja) that is now largely part of Moldova and Ukraine (Article 11) -- may apply to reacquire Romanian citizenship. Descendants qualify to the second degree under Article 10 and to the third degree under the broader Article 11.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Historical civil-status and citizenship documentation establishing the applicant's own or an ancestor's prior Romanian citizenship and the chain of descent.

requirement_groups.name: Article 10 -- former citizens who lost citizenship voluntarily, and descendants to the 2nd degree

requirements.blocker_text: The applicant, or an ancestor up to the second degree, was formerly a Romanian citizen who lost that citizenship while acquiring or retaining a foreign nationality.

Must meet Article 8(1) letters b-e: loyalty to the Romanian state, legal means of subsistence, good conduct, and (since Law 14/2025) Romanian language knowledge at B1 level, except applicants over 65.

requirement_groups.name: Article 11 -- citizens dispossessed involuntarily (territorial changes), and descendants to the 3rd degree

requirements.blocker_text: The applicant, or an ancestor up to the third degree, had Romanian citizenship taken away or lost it for reasons not attributable to them (this is the route used chiefly by descendants of people in territories that were part of the Kingdom of Romania before 1940 and are now largely in Moldova and Ukraine).

Must meet Article 8(1) letters b-e: loyalty to the Romanian state, legal means of subsistence, good conduct, and (since Law 14/2025) Romanian language knowledge at B1 level, except applicants over 65.

evidence_required.document: Historical civil-status documents establishing the applicant's or ancestor's prior Romanian citizenship
Chain-of-descent documentation (birth/marriage certificates linking applicant to the qualifying ancestor)
Romanian language certification (B1), except applicants over 65
Original or certified multilingual document extracts issued within the prior 2 years (per Law 14/2025)

outcome.physical_presence_requirement: no residence in Romania is required to apply under this route

sources.title: Refworld (UNHCR) -- Romanian Citizenship Law 21/1991 (English translation, consolidated as of May 2025), Articles 10-11: reacquisition for former citizens (Art. 10, descendants to 2nd degree, voluntary loss) and for those involuntarily dispossessed including via territorial change (Art. 11, descendants to 3rd degree), both subject to Article 8(1)(b)-(e) conditions plus Romanian language proof

Transilvania University of Brasov (academic law review) -- analysis of Law 14/2025's amendments to Law 21/1991: mandatory B1 Romanian language proof for reacquisition applicants (waived over 65), 2-year document-freshness rule, mandatory biometrics from 25 July 2024, processing timeframe extended from 5 months to up to 2 years 6 months, automatic rejection where document authenticity is in doubt

Immigrant Invest (relocation consultancy) -- Romanian citizenship repatriation route for descendants of people who lived in the Kingdom of Romania 1918-1940, covering modern-day Moldova and parts of Ukraine; described 2-5 year process, consulate filing, oath of allegiance

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Romania). STATUS: DRAFT -- same tier-2-primary sourcing constraint as the other citizenship files (Romania's tier-1 legislative portal and the National Authority for Citizenship's own site were both unreachable across repeated attempts in this pass). THIS IS THE SINGLE MOST DISTINCTIVE AND CONSEQUENTIAL ROUTE IN THIS BUILD: Article 11 in particular is the legal basis for what is, in practice, one of the largest citizenship-reacquisition-by-descent programs in Europe by volume -- hundreds of thousands of citizens of the Republic of Moldova (and smaller numbers from Ukraine's Chernivtsi/Bukovina and other formerly-Romanian regions) have reacquired Romanian, and therefore EU, citizenship this way since the 1990s, without ever residing in Romania. No residence requirement applies to this route -- a structural feature this dataset's schema captures via 'physical_presence_requirement'. MAJOR RECENT DEVELOPMENT, FLAGGED: Law 14/2025 (effective in stages from July 2024) made this route substantially harder -- mandatory B1 Romanian language testing (previously assessed more loosely), a 2-year document-freshness window, tighter authenticity scrutiny with automatic rejection on unresolved doubt, and processing time extended from a statutory 5 months to up to 2 years 6 months. Combined with the sourced-but-unverified naturalisation approval-rate collapse noted in ro_citizenship_naturalisation.json, this suggests a broad, government-driven tightening across ALL discretionary citizenship routes in Romania as of 2024-2025, not isolated to reacquisition -- disclosed as a pattern worth independent verification against ANC's (National Authority for Citizenship) own published statistics, which could not be reached in this pass. The Article 10 vs Article 11 distinction (2nd degree/voluntary loss vs. 3rd degree/involuntary-territorial loss) is modeled as two separate requirement groups (OR logic) because they are materially different eligibility tests, not because they lead to different outcomes.
